title: Balloons
description: A celebration effect: glossy balloons float up and away, or a few words rise as letter balloons, over the page or contained in one element.

loop.script: click[0] → wait → wait → wait → click[1] → wait → wait → wait

props.name: balloons(options?)
props.type: (options?: { container?: HTMLElement | null; signal?: AbortSignal; reducedMotion?: "fade" | "skip" }) => Promise<void>
props.description: Releases a bunch of balloons sized to the viewport (or the container). Resolves when the last one has floated away, about 30 s later.

props.name: textBalloons(lines, options?)
props.type: (lines: { text: string; color: string; fontSize: number }[], options?: { container?, signal?, reducedMotion?, fontFace?: string }) => Promise<void>
props.description: Floats each line up as one balloon per character (emoji included), a second apart. fontFace is an @font-face rule with a data: URL.

props.name: useBalloons(options?)
props.type: (options?: { containerRef?: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>; reducedMotion?; fontFace? }) => { release, releaseText, stop }
props.description: The same functions bound to a component: contained in containerRef when given, and stopped when the component unmounts. Each call can pass its own signal.

props.name: balloonFontFace(family, url)
props.type: (family: string, url: string, descriptors?: string) => Promise<string>
props.description: Fetches a font file and returns the @font-face rule (as a data: URL) that textBalloons embeds in each letter.

props.name: --balloons-font-family
props.description: The text balloons' font family, read from the container (or the root element) when they are released.

a11y: Decorative: every layer is aria-hidden and pointer-events: none, so the page stays usable while balloons fly. Announce the success itself in text.
Reduced motion (WCAG 2.3.3): no balloon moves. By default one still frame of the effect fades in and out over 2.4 s (opacity only); reducedMotion: "skip" does nothing.
The effect runs once per call and is over in seconds on screen (2.2.2 needs no pause control); the wall's looping tile honours the gallery's pause and reduced motion.
